finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or authorization. The org to query comes straight from the request, so any caller can list the id and name of every user in any organization (broken access control / IDOR). Caveat: req.pg is never set in this file. It must come from middleware that isn't present, so reachability depends on code outside this repo. The auth gap holds either way, because no auth middleware is registered anywhere in the file.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request, query parameter `org` (req.query.org), db.js:9
finding.sink: req.pg.query('SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1', [req.query.org]), returned via res.json(rows), db.js:9-10

trace.note: express app created; no app.use() for authentication, session or tenant-scoping middleware
route /users registered with no auth guard
req.query.org used as the tenant filter with no check that it matches the caller's own org
app.listen(3002) binds on all interfaces by default, so the route is publicly reachable

finding.guards_checked: SQL injection: ruled out, because the query is parameterized with $1. Authentication and tenant checks: none found in the file. External middleware: none visible, and req.pg is assumed to be injected by code not in this repo. Also reviewed and found not exploitable: /file (path.resolve plus a startsWith(ROOT + path.sep) check blocks traversal) and /count (execFile with a fixed argument array, no user input).

verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: db.js:8-10 has no auth guard, uses req.query.org as the tenant filter, and db.js:23 listens on all interfaces. However, req.pg is never set in the only source file, and no app.use() exists, so as written db.js:9 would throw a TypeError. Whether the route works, and whether an upstream gateway or middleware supplies auth or tenant scoping, can't be determined from this repo.
